card.title: Try it — fully offline
card.subtitle: Ships with a recorded session and everything it generated

narration.text: Making a demo video used to cost me a whole day.
Then I found one that reads the terminal session I already have.
Point it at a recording — asciinema, vhs, whatever.
It reads the session and works out what got demonstrated.
Then it designs the whole timeline around that.
The hard part is the music — models can't be told where a beat goes.
So it generates several candidates and measures every one.
The cuts land on the beats it actually finds.
Narration works the same way — synthesize, measure, place.
When narration overruns, the shot stretches to fit it.
When it can't stretch, the line goes back for a rewrite.
You get reel.mp4 — and the timeline itself, reel.otio.
It opens in a real editor. Every clip its own. Narration and music on separate tracks.
Cut points sit where the beats are. No guessing.
Ships with a recording and everything it generated.
First run: no API key, no network, no Python.
